Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	Reject the null hypothesis; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll. Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	Fail to reject the null hypothesis; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect

Incorrect	The null hypothesis is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct

The null hypothesis is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><caption style="text-align: left; font-weight: bold; padding: 6px;">Chi-square critical values (probability in the right tail)</caption><thead><tr style="background: #e3e8ed;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; ">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 1.25.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	Reject the null hypothesis; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The null hypothesis is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect

Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The null hypothesis is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect

Incorrect	The null hypothesis is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct

The null hypothesis is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><caption style="text-align: left; font-weight: bold; padding: 6px;">Chi-square critical values (probability in the right tail)</caption><thead><tr style="background: #e3e8ed;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; ">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 0.67.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	Reject the null hypothesis; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct

20.00</strong></td></tr></tbody></table><p>You roll a six-sided die 60 times. The null hypothesis is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><caption style="text-align: left; font-weight: bold; padding: 6px;">Chi-square critical values (probability in the right tail)</caption><thead><tr style="background: #e3e8ed;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; ">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 20.00.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	Fail to reject the null hypothesis; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct

Incorrect	The null hypothesis is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	Fail to reject the null hypothesis; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect

Correct	The null hypothesis is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll. Correct	The null hypothesis is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll. Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The null hypothesis is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect

Incorrect	The null hypothesis is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The null hypothesis is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect

Correct	The null hypothesis is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect

24.00</strong></td></tr></tbody></table><p>You roll a six-sided die 72 times. The null hypothesis is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><caption style="text-align: left; font-weight: bold; padding: 6px;">Chi-square critical values (probability in the right tail)</caption><thead><tr style="background: #e3e8ed;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; ">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 24.00.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	The null hypothesis is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	Fail to reject the null hypothesis; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect

1.00</strong></td></tr></tbody></table><p>You roll a six-sided die 60 times. The null hypothesis is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><caption style="text-align: left; font-weight: bold; padding: 6px;">Chi-square critical values (probability in the right tail)</caption><thead><tr style="background: #e3e8ed;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; ">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 1.00.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	The null hypothesis is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct

Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct

Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><caption style="text-align: left; font-weight: bold; padding: 6px;">Chi-square critical values (probability in the right tail)</caption><thead><tr style="background: #e3e8ed;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; ">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 7.25.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	Reject the null hypothesis; there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis; there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct
